policy.rule: Quantitative public claims require retained evidence, an exact metric and denominator, provenance, and limitations.

claims.allowed_wording: Plasmate compiles supported web pages into a structured Semantic Object Model (SOM).
limitations: Retained content and supported behavior depend on the page and configuration.

claims.allowed_wording: The retained v0.5.1 non-JavaScript public-web snapshot, generated 2026-07-19, recorded a 9.98x median serialized-byte ratio over 83 successful inputs from 98 attempted URLs.
limitations: Legacy artifact without current commit, corpus-digest, or runner provenance.
Serialized-byte ratio, not a token, cost, latency, memory, or task-success result.
Statistic is over successful inputs; blocked and failed inputs remain in the attempted-input denominator.

claims.allowed_wording: The retained v0.5.1 JavaScript-enabled public-web snapshot, generated 2026-06-07, recorded a 9.32x median serialized-byte ratio over 82 successful inputs from 98 attempted URLs.
limitations: Legacy artifact without current commit, corpus-digest, or runner provenance.
Serialized-byte ratio, not a token, cost, latency, memory, or task-success result.
Statistic is over successful inputs; blocked and failed inputs remain in the attempted-input denominator.

claims.allowed_wording: Plasmate provides a CDP compatibility layer for the supported Puppeteer/CDP workflows and methods documented in the README.
limitations: Not full CDP, Puppeteer, Playwright, Chromium, or web-platform compatibility.
The historical campfire-commerce pass validates one fixture and its listed assertions.

claims.allowed_wording: Plasmate documents integrations across AI and developer tools.
limitations: Directory inclusion does not establish current maintenance, end-to-end testing, or compatibility with every upstream version.
Do not publish a numeric integration count without a dated manifest defining inclusion and verification criteria.

claims.reason: The retained evidence does not establish universal token, cost, speed, or memory results. Measure those outcomes with a named tokenizer/model, comparable workload, build, runner, cache state, and complete denominator.
